name: Long-term Residence (Residencia de Larga Duración)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 5 continuous years of legal residence in Spain. Permitted absences: no more than 6 months continuous, or 10 months cumulative over the 5 years (18 months if work-related).

evidence_required.document: 5 years of continuous residence evidence, including full absence history

outcome.duration_length: indefinite status; the physical TIE card is renewed every 5 years (10 years from age 30)
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: max 6 months continuous absence, or 10 months cumulative over the qualifying 5 years (18 months if work-related)

sources.title: BOE — Real Decreto 1155/2024, larga duración provisions

notes: Spain's ILR-equivalent hub route, same structural role as uk_ilr, de_niederlassungserlaubnis, nl_permanent_residence, and pt_permanent_residence. Two modalities exist: larga duración NACIONAL (Spain only, simpler) and larga duración-UE (EU Directive 2003/109/CE, enables simplified intra-EU mobility but requires proof of stable sufficient resources) — modeled as a single route here since the qualifying conditions and core outcome are the same, same scope decision as the Netherlands' equivalent route. citizenship_after_months (60) reflects the GENERAL 10-year naturalisation track MINUS the 5 years already spent reaching PR — Ibero-American/Sephardic/family-tie holders would reach citizenship faster via es_naturalisation's other groups, not captured in this single route-level figure since PR itself doesn't discriminate by the applicant's eventual naturalisation track. Other qualifying paths to this status not modeled as separate requirement groups here (retirement/disability pensioners, born in Spain + 3 years post-majority residence, former Spaniards by origin, refugees/subsidiary-protection holders, 5-year wards of a Spanish entity, notable economic/cultural contribution) — flagged as a real scope simplification, since the standard 5-year residence path covers the large majority of cases in this dataset's use case.
